items.body_excerpt:
NRL Casualty Ward: Panthers' Yeo blow; Tupouniua sidelined again
Panthers skipper Isaah Yeo left the field in the first half at Go Media Stadium on Friday night with a suspected pectoral injury.
Yeo went in to make a tackle and immediately reached for his shoulder and had a shocked look on his face as he reeled away.
The NSW and Australian captain left the field in the 34th minute and cut a forlorn figure on the Panthers bench in the second term. He will be sent for scans to confirm the severity of the injury.
Before the game, Panthers centre Casey McLean had surgery on a fractured hand but is expected to miss only 1-2 matches.
McLean suffered the injury during Saturday's game against the Raiders in Mudgee and left the field with 20 minutes to play.
The injury to McLean saw three-time premiership winner Izack Tago promoted to the starting side for Friday night's bumper clash with the Warriors.
In Friday's second game, Roosters fullback James Tedesco missed the Round 23 blockbuster against the Bulldogs after failing to overcome an ankle injury.
Tedesco sat out the second half of the Round 22 slaughter of the Cowboys with ice on his ankle but he was initially named to return against the Bulldogs.
The skipper dropped out of the side on Thursday and has been replaced by Cody Ramsey.
However, it was another blow for Bulldogs star back-rower Sitili Tupouniua who was back from a hamstring injury, but was ruled out in his return game - again with a hamstring injury.
"Not sure how bad it is, but he's felt it in the same spot where he injured about eight weeks ago, so not ideal," Bulldogs coach Cameron Ciraldo said after the game.
"He's pretty devastated because he was training really well and he was just excited to get back playing, this is what he does, this is what he loves doing, so he's pretty shattered."
The Knights suffered a blow ahead of Sunday's trip to Canberra with star centre Bradman Best dropping out with a calf strain suffered in last week's win over Brisbane.
Manly prop Ethan Bullemor suffered a head knock in training and will follow NRL concussion protocol. He will be stood down for 11 days meaning he will miss this week's clash against the Storm and next Friday's game against the Dolphins.
The Sea Eagles have also lost back-rower Kobe Hetherington for the remainder of the season after he suffered a ruptured bicep in training on Monday. He will undergo surgery next week.

Storm vs Sea Eagles Predictions & Tips: NRL Round 23 2026
Unchartered territory
The Storm were defeated 36-22 at home by the Bulldogs last week, all but ending their hopes of participating in the NRL Finals. It is an unusual feeling for the Storm as it is the first time this has occurred for coach Bellamy outside of the salary cap drama. They were flat at times in that match too. With an equal share of possession and the same completion rate as their opponent (76%), they made just 7.6m per carry and created just 4 line breaks. Uncharacteristically, they were poor defensively as they allowed 9.5m per carry, 9 line breaks, and 535 PCM’s.
A miserable week off
The Sea Eagles had a week out of the spotlight with the Bye following their embarrassing 48-12 loss at home to the Sharks. In a day to forget, they were left chasing the standard of their opponent for 80 minutes. The game was all but over as they trailed 30-6 at HT. with just 47% possession and a 77% completion rate, they averaged 8.8m per carry but only managed 1 line break. They were poor defensively also, missing 42 tackles and conceding 12 line breaks. If they are to climb back into the Top 8, they need to forget that performance and reset ahead of this contest.

Team Announcement: Round 23 v Manly
Craig Bellamy has named his Melbourne Storm squad for Saturday’s Indigenous Round game against Manly at HBF Park in Perth.
Bellamy’s team has been bolstered by the return of five-eighth Cameron Munster who has been named to start following his knee surgery, joining Hayden Watson in the halves.
Jack Howarth also returns to the number three jersey following his unavailability in Round 22 and will play his 50th Melbourne Storm game.
Tyran Wishart switches to hooker in place of Trent Toelau who shifts to the bench.
Alec MacDonald misses the game due to Round 22 concussion protocols.
The extended reserves includes last week’s try-scorer and rookie forward Angus Hinchey, alongside a potential return for hooker Gabriel Satrick.
Melbourne Storm will wear its 2026 Indigenous Round jersey, click here to learn more about the design, inspired by Gabriel Satrick's journey to the NRL.
Saturday’s game kicks-off at 1pm (AWST), 3pm (AEST) with tickets available here .
Fans in Perth are encouraged to come along to Friday’s Open Training Session at HBF Park, with gates opening at 9:30am.
The game is supported by Tourism Western Australia, Venues West and Perth Bears.
